rationale: Unblinded primary-dysmenorrhea trial adding oral whole turmeric powder to naproxen reports VAS decrease 7.0 vs 5.6 (p<.001), but conflicts with linked registry NCT04183556 (90 actual crossover vs 149 parallel) and prints an implausible Table 1 SD.

Double-blind placebo-controlled 12-week RCT in overweight/obese adults with coronary slow flow phenomenon (PMID39085864, PMC11290174, IRCT20131125015536N8; 50 randomized, 42 completers) found 80 mg/day formulated nano-curcumin soft-gels improved secondary SF-36 Bodily Pain (+13.9 +- 15.3 vs -2.4 +- 9.3, between-group and ANCOVA p<.001); formulated nano-curcumin with vitamin E/C and polysorbate, non-Parkinson cohort, and 16% completer attrition without ITT.

Double-blind pilot of 3 g/day whole turmeric powder capsules vs placebo in hand osteoarthritis found inconclusive primary 1-month and between-group pain contrasts at all visits; 3-month p=.032/.017 are within-arm vs baseline with baseline imbalance.

Formulated Turmipure Gold trial (NCT04946981, n=44) had inconclusive primary 72 h soreness AUC; standardized curcumin extract in digestive complaints (DOI10.1186/s12906-021-03220-6) gave unclear SF-36 pain contrast; BCM-95 RA trial (PMID22407780) lacked placebo.

Ground turmeric chronic-pain crossover (PMID41599836, n=29) gave turmeric to both arms to test black pepper addition (p=.157); Mediterranean-diet pilot (PMID37521415), Herbagut (PMID29554961), and ZAZ2 (PMID21687764) did not isolate ground turmeric.

Oral, intrathecal, and injected isolated curcumin (PMID16584726, PMID29339457, PMID32171311) and combined ginger-turmeric extract (PMID32839804) reduced evoked rodent nociception without testing whole ground turmeric or Parkinson pain.

PD supplement survey (PMID36839160 pooled composite), PRIME-NL exposure survey (PMID38943398), Brasilia interview (ambiguous acafrao term), herbalist survey (tel-03267487), and Barbados/Mekong traditional surveys give no isolated ground-turmeric pain estimate.

English P1266 and French poster 12 match the same 39-person axial spondyloarthritis survey. Participants reported less pain with turmeric, without a known preparation, separate count, effect size or controlled contrast. Most received biologics.

Four placebo-controlled knee osteoarthritis trials favored turmeric formulations by 0.72 on a 0–10 pain scale (95% CI 0.06 to 1.39 points lower). Low certainty and below the authors' 1.5-point clinical threshold. Synthesis adds no independent vote.

The primary 100-mm VAS improved by 14.41 versus 6.02 mm with a proprietary extract versus placebo at day 90. The knee cohort and extract differ from the frozen comparison, and overlap with the pooled source remains unverified.
Parkinson add-on pilot randomized 30 per arm and published aggregate scores in the abstract. The separate pain or discomfort item and its direction were not reported.
